activities.caption: scrub the long-prose milestones the form grew from
activities.name: novelLongTimeline

events.title: Tale of Genji
events.text: Lady Murasaki, early eleventh-century Japan — arguably the first psychological novel, centuries before Cervantes.

events.title: Don Quixote, part one
events.text: Cervantes' parody of chivalric romance (part two follows in 1615, with the characters hearing about part one) — ordinary people, an interior life, a narrator who knows more than his characters.

events.title: Robinson Crusoe
events.text: Defoe's fake memoir so convincing that many first readers took it for fact — realism arriving as verisimilitude of document.

events.title: Pamela
events.text: Richardson tells the story in letters — epistolary form, psychology written from inside the moment.

events.title: Tom Jones
events.text: Fielding replies with an omniscient, ironic narrator conducting a meticulously plotted comedy.

activities.anchor: This device let the classic novel report a mind
activities.caption: find the line the syntax refutes
activities.name: novelFisSpot

config.prompt: One line of this Emma analysis is wrong — click it:
lines: "Emma Woodhouse, handsome, clever, and rich…" opens inside the narrator's third-person grammar.
"The real evils, indeed, of Emma's situation…" slides into Emma's own idiom without quotation marks.
The praise is the narrator's own settled judgement, held safely apart from the heroine's self-image.
The irony needs no commentary because the syntax delivers it.
The device runs from Austen through Flaubert to almost every third-person novel on a modern shelf.
config.correction: The praise is Emma's own self-image leaking through the narrator's grammar — the device lets the novel report a mind and judge it in the same breath.
config.why: Third-person narration that slides into a character's vocabulary and judgements without quotation marks — Austen's quiet revolution.

activities.anchor: Shape is how the causal chain is bent
activities.caption: rebuild the classical arc, stage by stage
activities.name: novelArcOrder

config.prompt: Rebuild the classical arc — the scaffold the novel kept and bent:
items: Destabilising event — where Pride and Prejudice's rich stranger insults its heroine in public, in the first scene
Climax and turn — Darcy's letter, the novel's hinge, where the reader's information flips
Resolution — the first proposal re-run under changed knowledge
config.why: The arc's name comes from Gustav Freytag's 1863 study of drama — a five-act inheritance the novel kept and bent.

activities.caption: call the size of the soliloquy
activities.name: novelMollyEstimate

config.prompt: Joyce's final chapter in Ulysses (1922) gives Molly Bloom a closing soliloquy. Roughly how many words does it run?
config.why: Roughly twenty thousand words — in eight enormous sentences: stream of consciousness rendering thought as it actually flows, associative and unpunctuated.
config.context: Woolf's Mrs Dalloway (1925) makes the same bet at party scale — the whole novel proceeds by way of its attendees' drifting minds.

activities.name: novelGlobalMatch

the form the empire brought, seized and turned on the empire

config.why: When We Were Birds (2022) brings Caribbean myth and graveyard magic into the same lineage Austen and Dickens built — the form absorbs everything and keeps growing.

activities.anchor: not a trick but a contract
activities.caption: walk the diagnostic on a suspect teller
activities.name: novelUnreliableBranch

config.root: You suspect the teller. Walk the diagnostic the contract implies.

start.text: Ishiguro's Stevens narrates in polished butler prose, repeating "dignity" and "professionalism" like a mantra while the events he reports undercut both. Your first move?

choices.label: Trust the diction — polished prose, polished man
choices.feedback: Taking the telling at face value.

choices.label: Hear the cracks — read against the teller
choices.feedback: Reading the gap between story and telling.

trust.text: The polish is the data: a first-person narrator is a character with limits, motives and blind spots, and the text plants enough evidence for you to read against him.

choices.label: Ask what kind of evidence licenses reading against the teller

cracks.text: The cracks in the diction are the evidence — the reader becomes a diagnostician, and the gap between story and telling becomes the novel's real subject.

choices.label: Ask what kind of evidence licenses reading against the teller

evidence.text: Planted evidence in the text — diction that lies by omission is enough. No confession is required: the unreliability is a contract between designer and reader, not a broken promise.

config.why: Narrators are constructed, not confided in — the novel is about what the polish hides.

config.text: "It is a truth %%0%% acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife" — and by the end of the paragraph the narrator's irony has flipped it into the neighbourhood mothers' wishful thinking.
config.hint: The adverb that makes the law-of-nature tone audible — and flippable.

activities.caption: drag the divider — scene time versus summary time
activities.name: novelDurationCompare

config.prompt: Narrative duration — drag the divider between the two gears:

before.label: Scene — minute by minute
before.text: A scene dramatised minute by minute: the duration ratio announces that what happens here is what the novelist thinks matters.

after.label: Summary — a decade in a sentence
after.text: Márquez spends a page on one execution and a sentence on seven decades — the ratio is the interpretation.

config.why: Duration is quantitative: the ratio of pages to days is a graph of the novelist's judgement.
